","char_count":613,"fact_ids":[],"source_anchors":[]},{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":3,"domain":"Illinois licensing programs fees","heading":"C — licensing programs fees","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Illinois licensing programs fees

FACT_ID: sec02-F01 | anchor: A01
A written driving-record request must identify the driver by full name, birth date and license number, include the fee and provide proper identification for the requester. [A01]
Why it matters: group Driving records; recall cue Identify driver and requester.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F02 | anchor: A01
Applicants aged sixteen or older are asked whether they want to join the Illinois organ and tissue donor registry. [A01]
Why it matters: group Application programs; recall cue Donor invitation begins at sixteen.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F03 | anchor: A01
An applicant requesting a veteran designation must document honorable military discharge, military retirement or service in the reserves or National Guard. [A01]
Why it matters: group Application programs; recall cue Veteran label needs service proof.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F04 | anchor: A01
Standard-credential applicants are told their voter-registration status and address, then asked whether to register or update an unregistered or outdated record. [A01]
Why it matters: group Application programs; recall cue Standard application offers registration update.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F05 | anchor: A01
A REAL ID applicant who proves United States citizenship is also applying for voter registration unless the applicant chooses to opt out. [A01]
Why it matters: group Application programs; recall cue Citizen REAL ID, registration unless declined.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F06 | anchor: A01
The agency sends voter-registration applications electronically to the state election board, which forwards them to the proper local election authority. [A01]
Why it matters: group Application programs; recall cue Application goes through election board.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F07 | anchor: A01
A person who is not a United States citizen cannot register to vote through a license application. [A01]
Why it matters: group Application programs; recall cue License eligibility is not voting eligibility.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F08 | anchor: A01
A Gold Star Family credential designation requires an affirmation of qualifying family membership naming the service member and the applicant’s relationship. [A01]
Why it matters: group Application programs; recall cue Gold Star affirmation names relationship.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F09 | anchor: A01
For a male applicant required to register with Selective Service, aged eighteen through twenty-five, signing the credential application certifies registration or authorizes the agency to submit it. [A01]
Why it matters: group Application programs; recall cue Qualifying signature authorizes registration.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F10 | anchor: A01
Illinois credential holders may supply emergency contacts and information about disabilities or special medical needs to a database used by police and emergency responders. [A01]
Why it matters: group Application programs; recall cue Emergency database supplies responder information.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F11 | anchor: A02
The handbook lists the instruction-permit application fee as twenty dollars. [A02]
Why it matters: group License fees; recall cue Permit fee, twenty dollars.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F12 | anchor: A02
The listed driver’s-license fee for applicants aged eighteen through twenty is five dollars. [A02]
Why it matters: group License fees; recall cue Young-adult license, five dollars.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F13 | anchor: A02
For a license applicant aged twenty-one through sixty-eight, the handbook lists a thirty-dollar fee. [A02]
Why it matters: group License fees; recall cue Ordinary adult band, thirty dollars.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F14 | anchor: A02
The license fee listed for ages sixty-nine through eighty is five dollars. [A02]
Why it matters: group License fees; recall cue Older adult band, five dollars.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F15 | anchor: A02
For ages eighty-one through eighty-six, the handbook lists a two-dollar license fee. [A02]
Why it matters: group License fees; recall cue Eighty-one through eighty-six, two dollars.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F16 | anchor: A02
A license applicant aged eighty-seven or older is listed as exempt from the license fee. [A02]
Why it matters: group License fees; recall cue Eighty-seven plus, no license fee.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F17 | anchor: A02
Adding a noncommercial license classification outside renewal costs five dollars; the table excludes commercial classifications from that entry. [A02]
Why it matters: group License fees; recall cue Off-renewal classification, five dollars.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-R01 | anchor: A01
The listed school-bus permit fee is four dollars. [A01]
Why it matters: group License fees; recall cue School-bus permit, four dollars.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-R02 | anchor: A01
Adding or renewing a motorcycle classification adds five dollars to the ordinary driver’s-license fee. [A01]
Why it matters: group License fees; recall cue Motorcycle classification adds fee.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-R03 | anchor: A01
The initial state identification-card fee is five dollars below eighteen and twenty dollars from eighteen through sixty-four, while ages sixty-five and older and persons with disabilities are listed as free. [A01]
Why it matters: group Identification fees; recall cue ID fee depends on age or disability.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-R04 | anchor: A01
A duplicate or corrected license or permit ordinarily costs five dollars, with two dollars listed for ages eighty-one through eighty-six and no fee for ages eighty-seven and older. [A01]
Why it matters: group Replacement fees; recall cue Replacement license has age exceptions.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-R05 | anchor: A01
A duplicate or corrected ninety-day temporary license is listed at five dollars, as is a duplicate or corrected Temporary Visitor Driver’s License. [A01]
Why it matters: group Replacement fees; recall cue Temporary credential replacement entry.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-R06 | anchor: A01
A stolen license or permit can be duplicated without charge for someone younger than sixty who provides a full police report; lost or stolen licenses or permits are free to duplicate at age sixty or older. [A01]
Why it matters: group Replacement fees; recall cue Sixty-plus license loss or theft, free duplicate.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-R07 | anchor: A01
A duplicate temporary ninety-day identification card costs five dollars, and the same listed fee applies to correcting that temporary card. [A01]
Why it matters: group Replacement fees; recall cue Temporary ID replacement or correction, five.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-R08 | anchor: A01
A duplicate identification card costs five dollars below eighteen and twenty dollars for ages eighteen through sixty-four, subject to the table’s free replacement provisions. [A01]
Why it matters: group Replacement fees; recall cue Duplicate ID has fee exceptions.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-R09 | anchor: A01
The table waives the duplicate identification-card fee for theft supported by a full police report, and for a lost or stolen card when the holder is at least sixty. [A01]
Why it matters: group Replacement fees; recall cue ID theft report or sixty-plus loss waiver.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-R10 | anchor: A01
A corrected identification card costs five dollars below eighteen, ten dollars from eighteen through sixty-four and nothing from sixty-five onward. [A01]
Why it matters: group Replacement fees; recall cue Corrected ID differs from duplicate ID.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-R11 | anchor: A01
Active Armed Forces members and the spouses and children living at home with them are listed as eligible for free duplicate licenses, permits and identification cards. [A01]
Why it matters: group Replacement fees; recall cue Active-service household duplicate waiver.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-R12 | anchor: A02
Credential fees can change through legislation, so the handbook directs readers to the agency’s website for current amounts. [A02]
Why it matters: group Fee and service limits; recall cue Fee table needs current verification.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-R13 | anchor: A02
Illinois no longer issues Temporary Visitor Driver’s Licenses beginning July first, two thousand twenty-four; a previously eligible applicant may seek a standard license. [A02]
Why it matters: group Fee and service limits; recall cue Legacy fee entry does not reopen issuance.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-R14 | anchor: A02
Eligible drivers can renew a valid license through the agency’s online services. [A02]
Why it matters: group Online services; recall cue Online license renewal requires eligibility.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-R15 | anchor: A02
The handbook lists online renewal of valid identification cards for ages twenty-two through sixty-four and says seniors aged sixty-five or older have free cards that do not expire. [A02]
Why it matters: group Online services; recall cue Online ID range and senior provision differ.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-R16 | anchor: A02
The agency’s online services include obtaining a driving-record abstract, renewing a plate sticker and filing business-service documents. [A02]
Why it matters: group Online services; recall cue Online services include records and plates.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-R17 | anchor: A02
Customers with administrative-hearing issues may contact the agency’s administrative-hearings email service. [A02]
Why it matters: group Online services; recall cue Hearing inquiries have an agency route.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]
